description: Hierarchical IW, HIW(`w_high`, `w_low`), plans on two levels: an IW(`w_high`) over a few high-level features, and below each high-level node its own IW(`w_low`) over the problem's features. A low-level search prunes states with the node's high-level features by low-level novelty, and hands up a state with other high-level features as a new high-level node if those features are novel at width `w_high`. Low-level searches pause at each new high-level node and resume round-robin, so a goal under an early high-level successor is found before the rest of its parent's search runs; the order is not breadth-first. If every high-level feature splits the state space into connected parts, like holding a key or not, HIW solves problems of width `w_high + w_low` while it expands at most `O(n_high^w_high · n_low^w_low)` states. Use it when you know a few such features and IW with a larger width would be too slow.

papers.authors: Miquel Junyent, Vicenç Gómez, Anders Jonsson
papers.title: Hierarchical Width-Based Planning and Learning
papers.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS 2021)

lineage.source: width-search, src/hiw.rs: "Without high-level features, HIW(`w_high`, `w_low`) is IW(`w_low`)."
